hints.title: Sliding Window of Fixed Size
hints.text: Every candidate subarray has exactly length k, making a fixed-size sliding window suitable.

hints.title: Frequency Contribution Delta
hints.text: When the frequency of an element increases from c to c + 1, subtract x^c and add x^(c + 1) to the running score modulo 10^9 + 7.

hints.title: Sliding Window Element Eviction
hints.text: When an element exits the window, adjust its power contribution similarly and update the maximum frequency score.

hints.title: Sliding Window Power Contribution Implementation
hints.text:
```python
from collections import Counter

class Solution:
    def maxFrequencyScore(self, nums: list[int], k: int) -> int:
        MOD = 10**9 + 7
        counts = Counter()
        cur_score = 0
        
        def add_val(x):
            nonlocal cur_score
            c = counts[x]
            if c > 0:
                cur_score = (cur_score - pow(x, c, MOD) + MOD) % MOD
            counts[x] += 1
            cur_score = (cur_score + pow(x, c + 1, MOD)) % MOD
            
        def remove_val(x):
            nonlocal cur_score
            c = counts[x]
            cur_score = (cur_score - pow(x, c, MOD) + MOD) % MOD
            counts[x] -= 1
            if counts[x] > 0:
                cur_score = (cur_score + pow(x, c - 1, MOD)) % MOD
                
        for i in range(k):
            add_val(nums[i])
        ans = cur_score
        for i in range(k, len(nums)):
            add_val(nums[i])
            remove_val(nums[i - k])
            ans = max(ans, cur_score)
        return ans
```

variables: max_c: maximum element frequency bounded by k
complexity.notes: Fixed window updates modular powers in logarithmic exponentiation time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Recomputing powers from scratch for each window position takes O(n * k * log k).
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: O(k) memory stores window frequency counts.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Maintains incremental delta updates to the running modular sum as elements slide.
